response.passage: Welcome to the City Zoo FAQ. Q: Who manages the zoo? A: Mr. Sharma, the head curator, oversees all operations since 2012. Q: Why are the nocturnal house lights dimmed during the day? A: The lights are dimmed because the animals are active at night, allowing visitors to observe their natural behavior in a simulated dark environment. Q: Can I feed the monkeys? A: No, feeding is strictly prohibited because human food causes digestive issues in primates. Q: How many species are currently housed here? A: We currently host 45 unique species in our enclosures. Q: Is the zoo open on public holidays? A: Yes, the zoo remains open on all public holidays, including Republic Day, to accommodate the high number of visitors. Q: Who is the famous visitor mentioned in our archives? A: In 1995, the renowned scientist Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam visited the facility to study the migratory patterns of birds. Q: Are the enclosures cleaned daily? A: Yes, the cleaning staff ensures that all 12 main zones are sanitized every morning before opening hours.
response.summary: This FAQ provides information about the management, operational rules, and history of the City Zoo. It clarifies visitor guidelines and explains the reasoning behind specific animal care practices.
